 Advertisement Iowa Democrats say election wins signal return to purple state
 Advertisement Updated: 5:46 PM CST Nov 4, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Todd Magel Anchor/Reporter Iowa Democrats say election wins signal return to purple state
 Updated: 5:46 PM CST Nov 4, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Todd Magel Anchor/Reporter DES MOINES, Iowa — Iowa Democrats celebrated election night victories at the State Historical Museum, declaring the state has returned to being politically purple with a mix of Democratic and Republican leadership. 
 "To Iowa Democrats, you’ve had a hard few years here in Iowa. But balanced government has been restored," said Rob Sand, Iowa’s governor-elect , as cheers erupted from the crowd. 
 Advertisement Democrats Rob Sand, Josh Turek, and Sarah Trone Garriott emphasized that Iowa is no longer a red state, attributing their success to voters seeking change. 
 "They just want things to get done. And I think what they’ve seen is that with one-party rule, for too long, they haven’t seen things happen the way they want them to. So maybe bringing in the other side a little bit will bring some balance back and actually get stuff done," said Jennifer Konfrst, a Democrat from Windsor Heights. 
 Sand will govern alongside a Republican-controlled legislature, while Democrat Josh Turek will join Republican Chuck Grassley in the Senate — a dynamic reminiscent of retired Senator Tom Harkin’s tenure. Harkin underscored the importance of balance in leadership. 
 "We’re going to have a great new governor. He started his political career as an intern in my office. So I’ve known Rob for a long time, a great guy. He’s going to be a fantastic governor," Harkin said. 
 IOWA ELECTION RESULTS 
 IOWA GOVERNOR | US SENATE 
 US HOUSE: District 1 | District 2 | District 3 | District 4 
 STATEWIDE RACES: Ag Secretary | Attorney General | Auditor | Secretary of State | Treasurer | Constitutional Amendment 1 
 IOWA LEGISLATURE: State Senate | State House 
 Former Iowa Governor Chet Culver also expressed confidence in Sand’s ability to unite the state. 
 "Most importantly, he’s a uniting guy. He’s really trying to bring us all together. And that’s what governors need to do. And I think he will govern the same way. He’ll put the people of Iowa first, and he’s going to be ready to deliver on day one," Culver said. 
 Former Iowa Attorney General Tom Miller noted that voters are tired of the divisive red-versus-blue dynamic. 
 "I think the quality of the Democratic candidates in the country, in Iowa has been very high. And this is a year when candidate quality really made a difference. Democrats have been hungry, we’ve worked, more people organizing. So it all came together, couldn’t be happier," Miller said. 
 Sand pledged to work with all Iowans, regardless of political affiliation. 
 "And remember, all of us together, our neighbors, our friends, we all have a job to do to make this state better and truer, not just redder and bluer. Let’s get to work," Sand said.
